morningLede: Western Australia's turn is no longer a one-run wobble: months-stock printed 8.3 this morning, the second consecutive rise off the 7.9 base (7.9→8.1→8.3), with active listings up 27% in 30 days (607→771) — the fastest build of any state, against a 20% ask-to-sold gap. Nationally the early-positioning story softened: the rolling sold base stalled at 11,148 while stock rebuilt to 13.7 months, a full round-trip of the week's tightening.
note: House views written each morning by the desk analyst from last night's run. Income and build-cost figures are APPROXIMATE external benchmarks (label them as such, or verify current figures with web search). Land figures are from the certified RLP dataset.

houseViews.view: Updated and escalated: yesterday we deferred; today's 8.3 print confirms two consecutive rises off the 7.9 base with actives 607→771 (+27% in 30 days), the fastest supply build in the country, against a 20% forward-priced gap ($1,039 asked vs $867 sold) and only 69% of stock priced. Vendors are stacking hope-priced inventory into a market whose exhaustion signatures we already flagged: Mandurah +98.6% last 12m with lots -35.7% over three years on thinning volume (37→33→22), Hilbert's second derivative fading 59.3%→27.8%, Byford's 40.6%→32.1%. Shift from caution to a mild underweight on WA stage stock; the 10-month breach is now the escalation trigger, not the confirmation trigger.
houseViews.falsifier: Months-stock printing back below 8 on the next two runs, or the ask-to-sold gap closing below 12% via sold $/m² rising rather than asks cutting.

houseViews.view: Maintained: the freeze deepened again — Sydney South West at 35.5 months (from 35.2) with a mere 5.5% ask-to-sold gap ($2,201 vs $2,087), the proof that honest pricing doesn't clear at $725k medians; only a price-level shift or demand shock does. Sydney Northwest remains the pure strike: 34.5 months, only 200 of 587 listings priced (34%), $2,412 asked vs $2,339 on the thin priced tail. NSW headline loosened again, 15.6→15.9, on actives building to 3,333.
houseViews.falsifier: Basin priced-share rising above 60% alongside corridor months-stock falling below 20 on rising sold counts, or NSW headline dropping back below 14 on stable listings.

houseViews.view: Maintained: VIC grinds looser — 17.0→17.1 on actives 6,648→6,735 — but remains the only deep, fully screenable market (6,432 of 6,735 priced, 95%, at a $395k median). The ask-to-sold gap widened slightly to ~19% ($848 vs $715/m²) and Melbourne North pushed to 21.5 months on 487 sales, so vendor hope is still delaying absorption. The mechanical case is unchanged: cheap, abundant, priced stock is where any late-2026 investor rotation lands, taken as volume rather than price — but see the trimmed policy view below.
houseViews.falsifier: VIC months-stock pushing past 20 with sold 12m rolling below ~4,000, ask-to-sold gap widening past 20% (now at the doorstep), or new-listing absorption failing to lift by Q1 2027.

houseViews.view: Maintained with one nuance: the demand desert is intact — Melbourne Peri-Urban 38.6 months on 125 annual sales, South Gippsland 32.2 on 103, Gippsland 26.4 on 66 — markets without buyers, not overpriced markets, given 644–770m² lots against $395k fringe alternatives and 17 months of metro choice. The nuance: West Gippsland improved 20.4→18.2 months on sales lifting 147→163, the belt's first genuine volume print; watch it, but one corridor doesn't break the avoid. No englobo, no stage stock; this belt clears last.
houseViews.falsifier: Belt sold volumes rising 50%+ per window (West Gippsland sustaining above ~180), or peri-urban months-stock falling below 25 without listings simply being withdrawn.

houseViews.market: Regional VIC hubs vs thin-print fallen angels (Ballarat/Bendigo/Darley)
houseViews.view: Maintained: trust the corridor, not the sub-10-sale suburb print. Darley stays the set's cleanest mix artefact — -48.2% last 12m on 6 sales with lot sizes up 124.5% — and the Bendigo suburb print (-29.3% on 8 sales, lots -29.9%) is the same noise. The corridors clear: Ballarat 490 annual sales at 9.5 months, Bendigo 300 at 9.9, both roughly half VIC's 17.1, at $309–320k the cheapest functioning volume markets in the state. Real regional weakness remains confined to low-volume satellites (Creswick -36.8% 3yr on 8 sales, Smythesdale -22.2% on 5).
houseViews.falsifier: Ballarat/Bendigo corridor months-stock rising above 14, or corridor sold $/m² printing negative on stable 250+ sale windows.

houseViews.view: Maintained: the loosening trend extended a fourth run — 6.1→6.3→6.4→6.6 months on actives 479→558 (+16% in 30 days) — still the tightest mainland market, but decelerating on schedule. Adelaide North is now pricing at or below clearing ($907/m² asked vs $911 sold at 5.7 months), the signature of a market with zero vendor fat left. The headline ~28% sold-$/m² growth stays composition-inflated (like-for-like ≈ +9.5%), and the $424k median is defended almost entirely via lot compression — Mount Barker -27.2% 3yr, Morphett Vale -32.6% — compression being the market's confession that the gross-price ceiling binds.
houseViews.falsifier: Stock above 10 months, incentive share rising two runs in a row, or lot compression stalling while sales volumes fall.

houseViews.view: Maintained at high conviction on unchanged prints: $/m² accelerated +52.2% then +96.3% to $1,027 (vs $344 three years ago) while lots compressed 37.9% in a year (-47% over three) and volume thinned 79→46→34 per window. A market doubling its rate while shrinking the product a third on falling volume is borrowing from the ceiling, not raising it — at $1,027/m² the compressed lot still prints $400k+ gross in a sub-$450k affordability market. Sell stage stock into this rate; do not underwrite englobo at these residuals.
houseViews.falsifier: Lot sizes stabilising while $/m² keeps rising on volume recovering above ~50 sales per window.

houseViews.view: Updated — conviction trimmed from 'rising' to 'intact but not yet confirmed': the sold base stalled (11,147→11,148 overnight) while months-stock completed a full round-trip 13.7→13.4→13.5→13.7 as actives built to 12,723. Over 30 days, absorption (+10.7% sold base) exactly matched the listings build (+10.7%), so the footprint now reads as demand keeping pace with supply, not outrunning it. The 1 Jul 2027 rotation thesis (negative gearing to new builds, CGT indexation) still directs any bid toward priced, cheap stock — VIC at 95% priced and $395k, QLD corridors, SA — not Sydney basins where 66% of Northwest stock cannot be screened; but 'early positioning' needs the sold base to resume growing against the build.
houseViews.falsifier: Sold 12m base flat-lining below ~11,300 through August while listings keep building, no pickup in VIC/QLD new-listing absorption by Q1 2027, or policy amendment before commencement.

houseViews.view: Maintained: the post-expansion base held a third run within band — asking $478.5k flat, $/m² $721→$723, actives 1,071→1,091, months-stock 9.0→9.3 — the expected settling after the 7-Jul universe expansion (948→1,022 suburbs). The underlying market remains the firmest large east-coast state: South Ripley +82% last 12m to $1,774/m² on a 33-sale window, Bahrs Scrub +53.4% to $1,319 on stable windows; Blacks Beach (+125%, lots +59%, 6 sales) stays quarantined as a mix artefact, as does Greenbank's +56.6% on a 6-sale sell-out tail (from 76). The $479k/9.3-month level is usable; the 30-day change series stays quarantined until August.
houseViews.falsifier: Like-for-like (pre-expansion suburb set) QLD asking or sold $/m² falling on the next monthly comparison, or the base failing to hold ±3% over the next fortnight.

houseViews.view: Maintained: capitulation clears, holdouts don't. St Leonards remains the healthy adjustment — -11.3% last 12m on 55 sales, nearly double the 28 of three years ago — and Torquay's bottoming stays on track (-12.6% prior year decelerating to -5.8% on 43 sales vs 10 three years ago). San Remo is still the holdout tell: decline accelerating -7.7%→-19.8% with volume thin at 15, meaning another leg down before it transacts; Cowes (-13.7% on 15) stays on the same watch-list.
houseViews.falsifier: Torquay/St Leonards volumes falling back below ~15–20 per window, or price declines re-accelerating past -10% in the high-volume priced coastal names.

policyCalendar.event: Negative gearing restricted to NEW BUILDS only; CGT 50% discount replaced by indexation (new-build investors keep choice). Expected to rotate investor demand toward new land/dwellings from late 2026.
Gifford Hill (Murray Bridge SA) first ~1,000 lots targeted for release, pending code amendment.
